insights.headline: Domestic gold, silver fall for a fourth session as a strong rupee blunts the global rebound
insights.summary: September gold imports plunged 81% YoY to $1.8 billion and silver 49% after May's duty hike to 15%, and Delhi dealers quoted gold at a discount of up to $6/oz as demand stayed sluggish ahead of Diwali. Global bullion edged higher on Friday, with COMEX gold around $4,178/oz, even as hot US CPI (3.7% YoY) and PPI (6.3% YoY) lifted Fed rate-hike odds. Indian buyers saw no relief: Delhi gold fell Rs 900 to Rs 1.49 lakh/10g and silver dropped Rs 6,000 to Rs 2.15 lakh/kg as the rupee strengthened to Rs 95.05.
points: September gold imports fell 81% YoY to $1.8 billion and silver 49% to $665 million, per Commerce Ministry data.
COMEX gold traded near $4,178/oz and silver near $57.43/oz on Friday, recovering from the midweek selloff.
Delhi gold fell for a fourth straight session to Rs 1.49 lakh/10g; silver dropped Rs 6,000 to Rs 2.15 lakh/kg.
The rupee strengthened for a fifth session to Rs 95.05 against the dollar, per PTI.
Mutual funds stopped bulk gold-ETF subscriptions ahead of the festive season; jewellery stocks rose up to 10%.

trending.title: India's buyers sit out the rebound
trending.summary: Global bullion recovered from its midweek selloff, but Indian demand stayed sluggish: imports collapsed, discounts persisted, and Delhi prices fell a fourth straight session on a strong rupee.

trending.title: Hot US inflation fails to sink gold twice
trending.summary: September CPI at 3.7% and PPI at 6.3% lifted Fed hike odds, yet gold climbed back toward $4,200 as a softer dollar and falling yields offset the rate pressure.

trending.title: Rupee rescue has a price
trending.summary: The rupee's fifth straight session of gains to 95.05 kept a lid on domestic gold and silver even as global prices rose, while forward hedging costs hit decade highs.

trending.title: Festive playbook: jewellers rally on ETF curbs
trending.summary: Jewellery stocks jumped up to 10% as mutual funds halted bulk gold-ETF subscriptions ahead of the festive season, with investors betting on Diwali demand.

items.summary: India's gold imports fell 81.27% year-on-year to $1.8 billion in September and silver imports fell 49.11% to $665 million, per Commerce Ministry trade data. For April-September, gold imports were down 27.32% at $19.27 billion and silver down 25.17% at $2.4 billion, after import duty was raised to 15% in May. The piece also notes the PM's call to defer gold purchases amid the West Asia crisis.
items.title: Gold imports plunge 81%, silver 49% in September: What is driving the fall
Gold, silver rebound in global trade: What investors should watch next
items.summary: Global bullion edged higher Friday — COMEX gold near $4,178/oz, silver near $57.43/oz. Delhi saw no relief: gold fell a fourth straight session to Rs 1.49 lakh/10g, silver dropped Rs 6,000 to Rs 2.15 lakh/kg as the rupee strengthened to Rs 95.05. IBJA's Kothari flagged silver support at $55-56/oz; VT Markets' Khoo put gold's levels to watch at $4,280 and $4,055.

items.title: Gold demand drops in India as prices rebound
items.summary: Indian physical gold demand stayed sluggish as domestic prices rebounded to about Rs 1,50,900/10g from last week's two-month low. Dealers quoted discounts of up to $6/oz over official prices, narrower than last week's $14, as a Mumbai dealer said softer imports were tightening supply. Consumers are pausing purchases ahead of Dussehra and Diwali.

items.title: Gold, silver futures gain up 1%; can this recovery sustain? Analyst view
items.summary: MCX gold futures traded at Rs 1,48,274/10g, up 0.53%, and silver futures gained 1.09% to Rs 2,12,956/kg, tracking international gold around $4,204/oz. Analyst Anuj Gupta says the dollar index slipping below 102 and steady US bond yields are the keys for the recovery to hold. Support cited: $4,107/oz globally and Rs 1,46,500/10g on MCX.

items.title: Gold rises towards $4,200 as bears lose their grip despite hotter US inflation
items.summary: US gold futures rose about 1.7% to $4,177.30 on Friday as falling Treasury yields and a softer dollar helped bullion shrug off hot September inflation (CPI 3.7% YoY, PPI 6.3% YoY). Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at the IMF-World Bank meetings, declined to prejudge the Oct 27-28 decision, cooling fears of a second straight hike. $4,200 is the key resistance.

Spot gold rose 0.2% to $4,177.82 an ounce by 0433 GMT on Friday but was down 0.5% on the week, as a softer dollar supported prices while the hottest US PPI reading in over four years and accelerating CPI kept Fed-hike risk alive. December gold futures gained 0.7% to $4,199.10 and spot silver rose 0.7% to $57.81. Markets priced a 28% chance of an October Fed hike and 89% for December.
items.title: Gold gains on softer dollar, but heads for weekly fall
PC Jeweller, Shanti Gold & other jewellery stocks rally up to 10%. Here's why
items.summary: Jewellery stocks surged on Friday after about 17 mutual fund houses temporarily barred fresh subscriptions to gold ETF Fund of Funds: Shanti Gold hit a 52-week high of Rs 421.85 (+7.6%), Sky Gold gained 6.1% to a record Rs 1,064 and PC Jeweller rose 9.9% to Rs 15.89. The October 15-16 curbs, per SEBI instructions via AMFI, don't affect redemptions. Analysts expect resilient festive demand.

items.title: Rupee relief comes with disruptions in financial markets
items.summary: The RBI's most aggressive rupee defence in over a decade has the currency set for a 1.9% weekly gain, its biggest in four years, but hedging costs jumped to a decade-high and bond yields to their highest in over three years. Saturday's rules require lenders to set aside 20% of the rupee equivalent of FX derivative deals above $2 million; 3-month forward yields hit 6.54%, highest since May 2016.

items.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
items.summary: Several large fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra, UTI and HDFC Mutual Fund, issued notices late on Thursday halting bulk subscriptions to their gold ETFs as festive-season demand picks up; redemptions are unaffected. The move followed a nudge from SEBI, and bullion dealers read it as a precautionary step to avoid an October import surge after September's Rs 4,451 crore of net ETF inflows.

FXEmpire's forecast notes spot gold has recovered toward $4,177 as falling Treasury yields fuel a rebound despite hot PPI data, with the metal consolidating between $4,100 and $4,220. A clear break below $4,100 would expose $4,000 support, while a move above $4,200-$4,250 resistance could open the 50-day average near $4,330; hawkish signals from Fed Chair Warsh could renew selling in both metals.
items.title: Gold and Silver Price Forecast: Falling Yields Fuel Rebound Despite Hot PPI
Gold Rallies With Treasuries as AI Selloff Boosts Haven Assets
items.summary: Gold extended its rebound in tandem with US Treasuries as a deepening selloff in AI-linked technology shares sent investors toward haven assets. The joint rally in bullion and bonds builds on Thursday's haven bid, when falling yields and a softer dollar lifted gold after hot US inflation data had revived Fed rate-hike bets.

Silver held steady in Indian retail trade on Friday at about Rs 2,300 per 10 grams in most cities (Rs 2,400 in Chennai, Hyderabad and Kerala), per Goodreturns data cited by HDFC Sky, after falling about 2.1% over the week to a two-week low. Jewellery stocks moved higher in morning trade, with Senco Gold up 3.6%, PN Gadgil 1.6% and Vaibhav Global 1.1%, while the rupee's gain also cushioned prices.
items.title: Silver Prices Hold Steady; Jewellery Stocks Rise
With inflation rising, will Warsh keep investors guessing?
items.summary: A Barron's column in Mint argues Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is deliberately withholding forward guidance even as September PPI posted its largest monthly gain in over four years, CPI ran at 3.7% and core CPI climbed to 2.6%, leaving markets guessing about the Fed's next move.

items.title: Fed's Goolsbee on inflation: discouraging, but still some optimism
items.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said this week's stronger-than-expected CPI and PPI readings were 'discouraging', per Reuters. He stayed cautiously optimistic if inflation proves temporary — tariffs, Middle East tensions, supply disruptions — but warned demand-driven pressure from AI data-centre buildouts would be 'more disturbing' and could require a policy response.

items.title: Comex Silver Settles 2.32% Higher at $56.837 — Data Talk
items.summary: Front-month COMEX silver for October delivery settled $1.29 (2.3%) higher at $56.84 on Thursday, snapping a three-session losing streak with its biggest one-day gain since October 9. The bounce tracked a softer dollar off an 18-month peak and a slide in Treasury yields to a three-week low, though silver remains down about 19% so far in 2026 and roughly half its January record.

items.title: Silver Output at Mexico's San Dimas Mine Fell 41%, and Now It Has Stopped
items.summary: First Majestic's San Dimas silver mine in Mexico is on formal strike since October 8, with about 800 union workers citing safety and contract breaches; extraction stays halted. The mine produced 41% less silver in Q3 than a year earlier, per the company's release, which blames 12 lost days and lower grades. More strikes would widen silver's forecast 46.3-million-ounce 2026 deficit.

items.title: DGFT Speeds Up Silver Imports Through IIBX & Nominated Agencies
items.summary: DGFT’s Trade Notice No. 30/2026-27 (13 October 2026) introduced a simplified, expedited procedure for silver import authorisations covering specified ITC(HS) codes, excluding silver dore. Applicants must declare imports at the generally applicable duty rate and justify quantities; each authorisation is valid for six months. Silver must be procured only through IIBX or nominated banks and agencies.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $57.50 amid safe-haven demand
items.summary: Silver rose for a second day to around $57.80/oz in Asian hours as an equity selloff revived haven demand, with Middle East tensions — a Houthi-Iran flare-up and a sunken Singapore-flagged ship in the Strait of Hormuz — in the background. TD Securities noted heavy CTA short-covering across rates, reversing Thursday's gold selling. FedWatch: 72% chance of a hold this month, 92% of a December hike.

items.title: MCX Gold trade above ₹1.47 lakh per 10 gram, Silver rebounds from ₹2.11 lakh support; check trade setup for Oct 15
items.summary: MCX gold December futures rose 1.4% to ₹1,47,916 per 10 grams as value buying returned after the hot-CPI selloff, aided by a softer dollar; silver December futures gained 1.3% to ₹2,11,119 per kg after rebounding off the ₹2.11 lakh support. The session piece maps key intraday support and resistance levels for Oct 15.
